title: Harmonica, mandolin and string bands; Bunker Johnson
summary: He recalls harmonica players and string bands, including an excursion in Louisiana.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: What about the harmonica players?
Well, they had some good harmonica players too, but they wasn't in bands though them days and times. Like they all know.
Yeah, what would they do, just walk around?
Yeah, the harmonica would play by themselves you know.
Serenading and strolling huh?
Yeah. They wasn't in no bands.

Let's see, what are some of those other things that they had like that? They must have had some more instruments. Hmm? They must have had some more instruments. What about mandolins? Did they use mandolins in their jazz bands?
Well, I never did play with a mandolin. I beat it with a little head of my time. But they used to play in bands though.
They used to have them in bands.
Yeah, but I never did play with nobody to play a mandolin yet.
Would they have a mandolin and a horn too? Or would it just be all strings?
I think all strings.
I see.
Guitars, violin, mandolins, and bass like that.
Did you ever see any mandolin players you remember?
Yeah, in the home of Louisiana I went one time to play on Excursion. I seen them with a violin and a mandolin and a guitar and a bass playing. And it sounded very good. Did you know them?
No, I didn't know them.

I didn't know them. That's the first time I've seen a bunker. I was in the country then. I was a little boy then, but I was playing music. And I went on Excursion to home in Louisiana and I stood by a bunker all day long, man. That's not even blow.
Who was he playing with? His own band? Yeah, his own band, yeah.
Bunker Johnson.
